walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 1: Performing and Appraising — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 1: Performing and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 1: Performing and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: It is always C major.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
They are the same scale.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
It is always C major.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
